title: Best Heist Thrillers to Stream
intro: The heist genre runs on a simple contract with its audience: show your audience the rules, then break them in a way nobody saw coming. The best of this list honours that contract. Some are operatic cons, some are granular procedurals - all of them reward full attention and punish second-screening.

picks.title: Money Heist (La Casa de Papel)
picks.one_line: A Spanish professor orchestrates the most theatrical bank robbery in television history - the first two parts are tight genre craft; the rest are spectacle that earned its loyal audience.

picks.title: Lupin
picks.one_line: Omar Sy as a gentleman thief working inside a real Paris - French verve, fleet plotting, and a lead performance that makes Arsène Lupin feel invented for 2021.

picks.title: Hustle (2022 film)
picks.one_line: Actually a sports drama but built on a con-film DNA - listed here for viewers who follow the heist genre for its underdog-outwitting-institutions emotional core.

picks.title: Farzi
picks.one_line: A street artist printing counterfeit currency and a lone-wolf cop closing in - Raj & DK make the premise both thrilling and funny, which is a harder trick than it looks.

picks.title: Now You See Me
picks.one_line: Four illusionist-thieves robbing banks during live shows while the FBI scrambles - the twist is telegraphed in retrospect, but the ride earns it.

picks.title: Inside Man (2023)
picks.one_line: Steven Moffat's BBC mini writes two timelines toward a collision - more psychological trap than physical heist, and smarter than its elevator pitch suggests.

picks.title: The Italian Job
picks.one_line: The gold-standard ensemble heist film: a Venice betrayal, a LA payback, and a Mini Cooper chase that became the genre's defining image.

faq.q: Is Money Heist worth watching all five parts?
faq.a: Parts 1 and 2 (the Royal Mint arc) are essential - tight, inventive, and built around a watertight plan. Parts 3-5 trade tightness for scale and emotion; they're worth it if you're invested in the characters, but the craft ceiling is lower. Many viewers treat the first arc as a self-contained series and stop there.

faq.q: Any Hindi-language heist content worth watching?
faq.a: Farzi on Prime Video is the most recent and most accomplished - Shahid Kapoor vs Vijay Sethupathi across a counterfeit-currency operation, directed by the people who made The Family Man. Scam 1992 on SonyLIV qualifies if financial fraud counts; it's arguably a better show than any of the fictional heist entries.
